title: Building Agentic Applications w/ Heroku Managed Inference and Agents — Julián Duque & Anush Dsouza
talk_summary: A Heroku workshop demos managed inference and an agent endpoint that runs native tools (code execution, Postgres schema/query, document conversion, dyno commands) and MCP servers on ephemeral one-off dynos. The transferable parts are read-only DB access, schema introspection before SQL, scale-to-zero tool sandboxes, MCP gateway exposure, and streaming long tool runs.

takeaways.technique: Read-only DB follower for agent SQL
takeaways.what_they_do: Heroku's Postgres tools only run against read-only follower databases; write access is left to self-deployed MCPs under user risk.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The posgress database tools only work on followers. Followers on Heroku are read only for security reasons.

takeaways.what_they_do: Agent calls a get-schema tool to retrieve the exact DB shape, then generates and runs a query instead of hallucinating schema.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it will get exactly what you have on the on the database and then we can pass that schema to the next tool which is run query

takeaways.what_they_do: The agent tool endpoint spins a one-off dyno for code execution or MCP, installs dependencies, runs, then scales back to zero.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It just spin ups, runs the code and it scales back to zero.

takeaways.what_they_do: Deploy MCP servers as apps, attach them to the agent endpoint, and also expose them via an authenticated remote SSE gateway for external clients.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all of the MCPS that I deploy to my app are going to be available through this endpoint

takeaways.what_they_do: The agent endpoint always streams because tool execution takes time; it emits tool calls and results as events.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all of the responses are a stream... because code execution access to database and this tool execution take time

takeaways.technique: Chain tools in one agent loop
takeaways.what_they_do: One agent run chains multiple tools, e.g. HTML-to-markdown then Python code execution, with inference over intermediate results.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we are going to use two tools... HTML to markdown and code execution Python
